He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]], where he was considered one of the top freshmen in 2013–14.[http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2014/01/syracuses_tyler_ennis_dukes_jabari_parker_have_been_top_freshmen_in_the_nation.html Duke's Jabari Parker, Syracuse's Tyler Ennis have been top freshmen in the nation][http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/01/17/freshman-tyler-ennis-syracuse-orange-jim-boeheim-pittsburgh/ Arguably nation’s most valuable freshman, Tyler Ennis leads No. 2 Syracuse] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140129214954/http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/01/17/freshman-tyler-ennis-syracuse-orange-jim-boeheim-pittsburgh/ |date=2014-01-29 }}[https://insider.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10365588/2014-nba-draft-tyler-ennis-vaults-top-10-nik-stauskas-debuts-no-14 2014 NBA draft Big Board 6.0] He was drafted 18th overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Ennis attended [[St. Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]]. Prior to heading south to St. Benedict's Prep, Ennis attended Cardinal Newman Catholic Elementary School in [[Brampton|Brampton, Ontario]], and [[Father Henry Carr Catholic Secondary School]] in [[Toronto]].[https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2014/01/17/tyler_ennis_of_brampton_best_freshman_point_guard_for_no_2_syracuse_orange_in_ncaa_basketball.html Tyler Ennis of Brampton, ‘best freshman point guard’ for No. 2 Syracuse Orange in NCAA basketball] In his junior year in 2011–12, Ennis led St. Benedict's, coached by Mark Taylor, to a school-record 35 victories and the No. 2 ranking in New Jersey. He was named the Gatorade New Jersey Player of the Year while averaging 14.6 points and 7.1 assists per game. In his senior year in 2012–13, the Gray Bees finished with a record of 31-2 as Ennis was honored as the Star-Ledger Prep Player of the Year and earned All-Prep First Team recognition after averaging 20 points, 6.1 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 3.1 steals per game.{{cite web|title=Tyler Ennis - 2013-14 Men's Basketball|url=http://cuse.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=10335|work=Cuse.com|access-date=May 15, 2014}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Ennis was listed as the No. 5 point guard and the No. 20 player in the nation in 2013.[https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/126967/tyler-ennis Tyler Ennis Recruiting Profile] ==College career== [[File:Tyler Ennis driving against Dayton.jpg|thumb|Tyler Ennis driving.]] In his freshman season at [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] in 2013–14, Ennis was named to the 2014 [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] second team, All-ACC Freshmen Team, and All-ACC Defensive Team. In 34 games, he averaged 12.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 2.1 steals in 35.7 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Tyler Ennis Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/tyler-ennis-1.html|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=May 15, 2014}} On February 28, 2014, Ennis was named one of the ten semi-finalists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx |work=NaismithAwards.com |access-date=February 28, 2014 |date=February 28, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006124015/http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }} Ennis helped lead the Syracuse Orange past Western Michigan in the second round of the 2014 NCAA Tournament,{{cite web|title=March Madness: Canadian Tyler Ennis leads Syracuse in win|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/march-madness-canadian-tyler-ennis-leads-syracuse-in-win-1.2579898|work=CBC.ca|access-date=March 22, 2014|date=March 20, 2014}} but missed a three-pointer at the buzzer of the following game that would have taken Syracuse past Dayton and into the Sweet Sixteen. ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2014–2015)=== On June 26, 2014, Ennis was selected with the 18th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]].[http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2014/06/26/phoenix-suns-select-tyler-ennis-with-18th-pick-in-nba-draft/11438393/ Phoenix Suns select Tyler Ennis with 18th pick in NBA draft] He later joined the Suns for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On August 8, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Suns.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-first-round-picks-t.j.-warren-and-tyler-ennis|title=Suns Sign First-Round Picks T.J. Warren and Tyler Ennis|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 8, 2014|access-date=August 8, 2014}} He made his NBA debut on October 29 in the Suns' season opener against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], recording two points, three assists and one block in a 119–99 win.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/LALPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Suns rout Lakers 119-99 despite Kobe's 31 points|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 30, 2014|access-date=November 14, 2014}} During his rookie season with the Suns, Ennis received multiple assignments to the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=2014-15 NBA Assignments |url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |access-date=January 22, 2015 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628235947/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=June 28, 2015 }} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2015–2016)=== On February 19, 2015, Ennis was traded, along with [[Miles Plumlee]], to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as part of a three-team deal involving the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]; as part of the deal, the Bucks also received [[Michael Carter-Williams]] from Philadelphia, while Phoenix received [[Brandon Knight (basketball)|Brandon Knight]] and [[Kendall Marshall]] from Milwaukee and Philadelphia received a future first-round pick from Phoenix.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-michael-carter-williams-tyler-ennis-and-miles-plumlee-three-team-trade|title=Bucks Acquire Michael Carter-Williams, Tyler Ennis and Miles Plumlee in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}} The next day, Ennis made his debut for the Bucks, recording four points and two assists off the bench in 89–81 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150220/DENMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Middleton, Henson lead Bucks to 89-81 win over Nuggets|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2015|access-date=February 20, 2015}} In May 2015, Ennis underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder.{{cite web|last=Gardner|first=Charles F.|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/bucks/tyler-ennis-getting-close-to-returning-from-shoulder-injury-b99606346z1-339183391.html|title=Tyler Ennis getting close to returning from shoulder injury|work=JSOnline.com|date=November 1, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2016}} On March 17, 2016, Ennis recorded career highs of 13 points and five rebounds in the Bucks' 96–86 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160317/MEMMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Ennis' big fourth lead Bucks past Grizzlies 96-86|work=NBA.com|date=March 17, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2016}} Nine days later, he recorded nine points and a career-high 12 assists in a 115–91 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/CHAMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Batum scores 25 as Hornets rout Bucks 115-91|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2016}} ===Houston Rockets (2016–2017)=== On September 22, 2016, Ennis was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Michael Beasley]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-complete-trade-milwaukee|title=Rockets Complete Trade with Milwaukee|work=NBA.com|date=September 22, 2016|access-date=September 22, 2016}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2017–2018)=== On February 23, 2017, Ennis was traded, along with the draft rights to [[Brad Newley]], to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Marcelo Huertas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170223-tyler-ennis-acquired|title=Lakers Acquire Tyler Ennis In Trade with Houson [sic]|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} On April 5, 2017, in his first start of the season, Ennis scored a career-high 19 points in place of injured starter [[D'Angelo Russell]] to lead the Lakers to a 102–95 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900548|title=Tyler Ennis scores 19 points, Lakers top Spurs 102-95|work=ESPN.com|date=April 5, 2017|access-date=April 5, 2017}} He surpassed that mark four days later, scoring 20 points in a 110–109 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900580|title=D'Angelo Russell sinks game-winning 3 after grandmother dies|work=ESPN.com|date=April 9, 2017|access-date=April 10, 2017}} On July 26, 2017, Ennis re-signed with the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/170726-tyler-ennis-signed|title=Lakers Sign Tyler Ennis|work=NBA.com|date=July 26, 2017|access-date=July 26, 2017}} On December 31, 2017, Ennis scored 20 points in a 148–142 double overtime loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975286|title=Paul helps Rockets to 148-142 win over Lakers in double OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2017|access-date=December 31, 2017}} On April 8, 2018, he scored a career-high 22 points in a 112–97 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]]. He shot 9 of 18 from the field, made three steals and played 28 minutes off the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975947|title=Jazz clinch playoff spot in crowded Western Conference|work=ESPN.com|date=April 8, 2018|access-date=April 8, 2018}} On June 28, 2018, Ennis was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180628-lakers-release-tyler-ennis|title=Lakers Waive Tyler Ennis|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2018|access-date=June 29, 2018}} ===Fenerbahçe (2018–2019)=== On July 19, 2018, Ennis signed a two-year deal with the Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]].{{cite web |title=Tyler Ennis joins Fenerbahce |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8vst5lmbq5mxu5qo/tyler-ennis-joins-fenerbahce |website=euroleague.net |access-date=19 July 2018}} In his first four games, he averaged 11.8 minutes and 6.7 points per game. Ennis suffered a severe ankle injury in a game on October 21 and was taken to the hospital.{{cite news |last1=Carlson |first1=Chris |title=Former Syracuse star Tyler Ennis taken to hospital after scary injury (report) |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2018/10/former_syracuse_star_tyler_ennis_taken_to_hospital_after_scary_injury_report.html |access-date=October 21, 2018 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=October 21, 2018}} His ankle was broken. On July 1, 2019, Ennis was released from the Turkish club. ===Raptors 905 (2019–2020)=== [[File:Tyler Ennis.jpg|thumb|left|Ennis in 2020]] On October 20, 2019, Ennis, who has spent time with four NBA teams, signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]], and was immediately waived. The moves were designed to make Ennis an affiliate player for the organization’s G League team, [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web |title=Tyler Ennis joins 905 |url=https://twitter.com/BlakeMurphyODC/status/1185920555029090309 |access-date=20 Oct 2019}} On November 20, he had a double-double of 23 points and 12 assists against the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{cite news |title=Tyler Ennis: Paces team in scoring |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tyler-ennis-paces-team-in-scoring/ |access-date=January 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=November 21, 2019}} On January 18, 2020, Ennis recorded 25 points, 10 assists, three rebounds and one steal in a 106-103 loss to the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite news |title=Tyler Ennis: Submits strong outing in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tyler-ennis-submits-strong-outing-in-g-league/ |access-date=January 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 19, 2020}} Ennis averaged 17.1 points, 7.4 assists, and 5.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Burrows |first1=Ben |title=Was leaving early the right choice for Tyus Battle? Syracuse basketball overseas and in the NBA G League |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/03/was-leaving-early-the-right-choice-for-tyus-battle-syracuse-basketball-overseas-and-in-the-nba-g-league.html |access-date=June 16, 2020 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=March 6, 2020}} ===Turk Telecom (2020–2022)=== On July 23, 2020, he has signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turk-telekom-officially-signs-tyler-ennis/|title=Turk Telekom officially signs Tyler Ennis|date=July 23, 2020|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 23, 2020}} Ennis tore his Achilles tendon on November 22, and was ruled out for the season.{{cite web |title=Turk Telekom Ankara guard Tyler Ennis suffers season-ending injury |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turk-telekom-ankara-guard-tyler-ennis-suffers-season-ending-injury/ |website=Sportando |access-date=November 22, 2020 |date=November 22, 2020}} ===Tofaş (2022–2023)=== On January 9, 2022, Ennis signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|BSL]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Tofas land Tyler Ennis |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/725633/Tofas-land-Tyler-Ennis |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 9, 2022 |date=January 9, 2022}} ===Napoli Basket (2023–2024)=== On September 3, 2023, he signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli Basket]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gevi-napoli-inks-tyler-ennis/|title=GeVi Napoli inks Tyler Ennis|last=|first=|date=September 3, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 3, 2023}} Ennis played in all 30 games that season, averaging 14.1 points, 4.2 rebounds, and a team-high 6.7 assists. Ennis helped Napoli win its first ever [[Italian Basketball Cup|Italian Cup]], scoring 21 points in the final against [[Olimpia Milano]].{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/legabasket/1631621/milano-napoli-final-eight-italian-cup-final-2024/|title=Napoli wrote HISTORY by winning the Italian Cup over a disastrous Milano|work=Eurohoops.net|first=Cesare|last=Milanti|date=May 7, 2024|accessdate=May 8, 2024}} ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2024)=== On May 6, 2024, it was announced that Ennis had been signed by [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] with less than five games to play in the regular season.{{cite web|url=https://www.syracuse.com/poststandard/2024/05/former-syracuse-basketball-player-tyler-ennis-signs-with-hapoel-tel-aviv.html|title=Former Syracuse basketball player Tyler Ennis signs with Hapoel Tel Aviv|work=[[The Post-Standard|Syracuse.com]]|first=Mike|last=Waters|date=May 7, 2024|accessdate=May 8, 2024}} ===Reyer Venezia (2024–2025)=== On June 18, 2024, he signed with [[Reyer Venezia]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite web|url=https://www.reyer.it/news/maschile/2024-06-18/ufficiale-tyler-ennis-e-un-giocatore-dellumana-reyer/|title=Ufficiale: Tyler Ennis è un giocatore dell'Umana Reyer|last=|first=|date=June 18, 2024|website=reyer.it|publisher=|language=it|access-date=June 18, 2024}} On February 6, 2025, Ennis was named Most Valuable Player of Round 18 of the 2024-2025 BKT EuroCup Regular Season. He had 19 points and 7 assists in a home win.{{cite web |title=Tyler Ennis wins the weekly MVP award heading to the Playoffs |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1781812/tyler-ennis-round-18-mvp-eurocup/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=13 February 2025 |language=en |date=6 February 2025}} ===Return to Hapoel Tel Aviv (2025–present)=== On July 1, 2025, he signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the Israeli [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Ligat HaAl]] for a second stint.{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/tyler-ennis-returns-to-hapoel-tel-aviv-on-two-year-deal/|title=Tyler Ennis Returns to Hapoel Tel Aviv on Two-Year Deal|date=July 9, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 10, 2025}} On January 6, 2026, Ennis suffered a torn [[achilles tendon]] during his team's win. It is the second Achilles tendon tear for him. He previously tore his during the 2020-2021 season.{{cite web |title=Hapoel Tel Aviv guard suffers Achilles tear |url=https://basketnews.com/news-238273-tyler-ennis-achilles-tear-hapoel-tel-aviv.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=7 January 2026 |language=en}} On April 16, 2026, the team decided to keep Ennis on the roster for the 2026-2027 season despite suffering a serious injury during the season.{{cite web |title=Hapoel retain Tyler Ennis for next season despite Achilles injury |url=https://basketnews.com/news-245178-hapoel-retain-tyler-ennis-for-next-season-despite-achilles-injury.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=16 April 2026 |language=en}} ==National team career== Ennis played for the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian men's national basketball team]] at the 2012 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], winning a bronze medal, and at the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]], leading the tournament in scoring with 20.9 points per game.[http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/07/syracuse_point_guard_tyler_enn_1.html Syracuse point guard Tyler Ennis led FIBA U-19 championship in scoring] In the 2012 tournament, he was a teammate of fellow college standout and eventual #1 pick of the [[2014 NBA draft]], [[Andrew Wiggins]].{{cite web |title=2012 FIBA Americas U18 Championship For Men – Canada |url=http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/7548/tid/257/_//index.html |work=FIBA.com |access-date=March
